To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

rearrangement and substitution reactions of homopentadienyllithium amide intermediates can be controlled by careful choice of reaction conditions and that the stereochemical outcome of the rearrangement can be controlled by choice of the substituents on the amine.

rearrangement and/or 1,3-substitution of one/two branched homopenta-dienyl groups in homopentadienyldiamines occurs on treatment with organolithium reagents, and that the reaction proceeds via a 1,2-shift of a branched homopentalienyllithium amido moiety with retention or via retro-pentadienyllithiation to form the corresponding imine.
the homopentadiene moiety in homopentadienes can be rearranged or substituted with good stereocontrol on treatment with organolithium reagents.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis and reactions of pentadienylamines, a class of compounds that have received little attention to date, and which are of interest for their potential as ligands for transition metal complexes and for use in organic synthesis.
the development of a novel synthetic methodology based on the use of organolithium reagents for the rearrangement and/or selective functionalization of homopentadienes.
the synthesis of 1,2- and 1,2,2-substituted 1-alkenylamines by the reaction of homopentadiene amines and organolithium reagents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reaction proceeds via a mixture of pathways, which can be controlled by careful choice of the reaction conditions.

the reaction of homopentadienyllithium amides with organolithium reagents is a complex reaction that can involve both substitution and/or rearrangement of pentadienyl group(s) depending on the structure of the starting homopentadienal amine and the experimental conditions employed.

the reaction of homopentadiene amines with organolithium reagents can be controlled to give either rearrangement, substitution, or a mixture of both depending on reaction conditions and substrate structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
homopentadienyllithium amides are configurationally labile, and the reaction outcome is dependent on both the organolithium reagents and the substrates.
homopentadienylation of amines is a powerful tool in the synthesis of a wide range of functionalized diamines, including 1,2- and 1,2,3-trisubstituted diamines.
the stereochemistry of the pentadienyl group is retained in the product when the reaction involves rearrangement, but not when substitution occurs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stereochemical outcome of the rearrangement is highly dependent upon the nature of the organolithium reagents employed.
the pentadienyl group can be used as a versatile and tunable building block in the design of new chiral ligands and catalysts for asymmetric synthesis.
organolithium reagents can be used to effect rearrangement and/or selective substitution of pentadienyl substituents in homopentadienylnitriles and -amines.
